mintAuthority.summary: Superstate controls native fund-share minting on Ethereum, Plume and Solana. EVM owner and proxy paths and the Solana mint key are centrally controlled; the public ledger is not independently reconciled against the full fund liabilities.
mintAuthority.headline: Issuer-controlled keys can mint native shares and replace EVM mint logic; public accounting does not establish independent whole-fund reconciliation.

review.evidence: The October 15 review independently identifies native owner minting, bulk minting and mutable EVM proxy paths at Ethereum block 26197388 and Plume block 99537544, plus the Solana mint authority at exact finalized slot 457209132. All three networks are explicitly native fund-share issuance in current issuer terms; EVM burn/reissue remains separately scoped in Bridge Risk and book-entry shares remain outside public token stock. USCC terms calculate NAV each business day from total assets less liabilities and prior-day outstanding shares adjusted for subscriptions and redemptions. Superstate's security page says ownership records overlap at the fund calculation agent, internally and on-chain. This establishes the disclosed internal-ledger workflow, not independent recurring whole-fund backing-to-liability reconciliation. The named NAV Fund Services calculation agent and Ernst & Young auditor do not establish a dated independent examiner's assurance scope, a current signed audit opinion or prudential supervision of USCC issuance. Therefore reconciliation is internal-ledger and supervision remains unknown rather than inheriting USTB's process labels. Exact mint-key custody and signing independence, independently reconciled native-token plus book-entry liabilities and the full default waterfall remain unavailable; these limitations do not erase the positively identified unbounded issuer mint paths.
